key_terms: The Hive service that accepts SQL sessions from clients such as Beeline and runs queries on an execution engine.
The service that stores metadata for databases, tables, columns, partitions and storage locations, without reading the data files themselves.
The filesystem or object-store location holding a table's actual data files, separate from the Metastore records that describe them.
A Hive table whose data files live at a declared location that Hive does not own, so dropping the table leaves the files in place.
The JDBC command-line client used to open a HiveServer2 session and run SQL.

worked_examples.title: Register an external table and one partition
worked_examples.interpretation: These statements from initialize.hql only write metadata to the PostgreSQL-backed metastore; no Parquet file is read or created. EXTERNAL means dropping the table later removes the definition but leaves the files. Partitions are not discovered automatically, so a new day directory stays invisible to queries until ALTER TABLE ADD PARTITION or MSCK REPAIR TABLE registers it.

worked_examples.title: Read metadata through Thrift without Beeline
worked_examples.interpretation: This simplified fragment from MetadataProbe.java talks directly to the metastore, so it works even when HiveServer2 is down. It should print file:/warehouse/orders and file:/warehouse/orders/day=2026-01-01. The probe also asks for a table that does not exist and expects an error, which shows the metastore answers truthfully rather than with a default. Seeing the right locations here while a Beeline query fails narrows the problem to HiveServer2 or the files, not the catalog.

evidence: Prepared actual Hive4.2.1/JDK21/PostgreSQL project; live SQL, independent Java Thrift, lifecycle, Iceberg and restore observations remain distinct acceptance gates.
